summary: The paper studies three training-free uncertainty-quantification signals (mean max-token-probability, negative predictive entropy, self-consistency) plus a logistic combination and a hidden-state probe for predicting correctness of a tiny (~50K-parameter) from-scratch transformer trained on integer addition, sidestepping the LLM-judge confound that plagues open-domain QA UQ evaluations. On the main seed=0 run (65.4% accuracy) all training-free signals discriminate well (AUROC 0.84-0.87), self-consistency is over-confident (ECE 0.088, reducible via calibration/combination), and confidence-based abstention raises retained-set accuracy to 81-90% depending on coverage. This round adds a new mid-scale (~31%-accuracy) 3-seed sweep responding to round-2 reviewers' critique that the prior 5-seed sweep ran at a near-degenerate ~3%-accuracy scale; the new sweep finds self-consistency's variance is no longer an outlier at higher accuracy, and the paper also corrects a table transcription error and explicitly flags two remaining gaps (no seed sweep at the 65%-accuracy scale, no bootstrap/DeLong CIs on the headline AUROC gaps).
strengths:
- All numerical claims I checked reproduce exactly against the included JSON logs: the main-run AUROCs (0.8712/0.8630/0.8408/0.8742 in results.json vs. 0.871/0.863/0.841/0.874 reported), the corrected neg-mean-entropy minimum (0.8384 in robustness_results.json vs. the corrected 0.838 in the text), the mid-scale sweep means/stds/values (robustness_midscale_results.json matches Table in Sec. 3 to 3+ decimal places), and the risk-coverage figures (I recomputed 1-risk from results.json's logistic_combo curve and got 0.906/0.878 at 50/55% coverage and 0.81 at 70% coverage, matching the abstract's "81%" and "high-80s at 50-55%" claims exactly).
- The paper is unusually transparent about its own limitations: it explicitly names the gaps reviewers raised (no full-scale seed sweep, no bootstrap CI), corrects a prior transcription error with a documented before/after value, and frames the new mid-scale sweep's conclusion appropriately hedged ("consistent with... though does not conclusively prove") rather than overclaiming that the instability question is closed.
- The core experimental design (ground-truth-exact synthetic arithmetic task to isolate UQ signal quality from judge quality) is a genuinely useful methodological contribution, cleanly motivated against the semantic-entropy/LLM-judge literature (Kuhn et al. 2023; Farquhar et al. 2024), and the full pipeline (code + logs + raw JSON for all three sweeps) is included and runs in real time on CPU, which I could verify directly.
weaknesses:
- The central open question — whether self-consistency's seed-instability is an artifact of near-degenerate accuracy or persists at the 65%-accuracy regime the headline numbers actually come from — is still unresolved after three review rounds. The paper's own framing states a full-scale sweep would take ~20 extra minutes of CPU time (well within the stated 1800s+ budgets these reviews typically allow), so the remaining gap looks more like a matter of the authors not having prioritized it than a genuine resource constraint, which weakens the credibility of "future work" as the closing move on the paper's own central methodological critique.
- The headline ranking (mean-max-prob 0.871 > entropy 0.863 > self-consistency 0.841) still has no significance test attached (the paper says so honestly), so the paper's own comparative claims about "mean-max-prob... slightly ahead" are not statistically supported by anything beyond a single seed's point estimate — a bootstrap CI over the existing eval-set predictions (which the paper says would only require reusing already-collected predictions, no new compute) was flagged as low-cost in round 2 and still wasn't done.
- The work remains restricted to a single synthetic task (integer addition) and a single tiny architecture; while this is explicitly scoped as a methods contribution rather than a claim about frontier LLMs, no second task with a different error structure (as one reviewer suggested) has been added, so the generalizability of the qualitative pattern (self-consistency variance shrinking with accuracy) beyond this one task is untested.
questions:
1. Given the paper states the full-scale (65%-accuracy) seed sweep would cost only ~20 minutes of additional CPU time, why was this not run for round 3 given it directly answers the paper's own central open question?
2. The bootstrap/DeLong CI on the single-seed headline AUROCs was also flagged as cheap (reusing existing predictions, no retraining) — what specifically blocked adding it this round?
3. Do you have any evidence (even informal) on whether the self-consistency variance-vs-accuracy relationship found here is monotonic, or could it non-monotonically re-diverge at higher accuracy (e.g., near-ceiling regimes where correct/incorrect samples are also imbalanced in the other direction)?
